info.title: PFF Premium Stats Pro CLI API
info.summary: Every operation the pff-pro CLI wraps: the original Premium Stats Pro API, mirrored under /v1, and PFF's own contract under /v2.
info.description:
The machine-readable contract for the `pff-pro` CLI, served public-read at `GET /openapi.json`
and `GET /openapi.yaml`. It describes the 59 read-only operations of the original Premium Stats Pro API
under `/v1` — league and game reference data, team and player reports, league-wide leaderboards and
PFF signature stats — and PFF's own operations under `/v2`, starting with the team page.

**Two surfaces, one document.** `servers[].url` is the bare origin, and every path key carries
its own version prefix. `/v1/...` mirrors the original Premium Stats Pro JSON API exactly — snake_case,
wire format untouched, the same reports the website has served for years. `/v2/...` is PFF's own
contract over the newer data — camelCase, a `columns` + `rows` table shape, and later a CSV form of
every table; `team-stats` is its first operation, the rest of the team page follows. Command names
come from `operationId`, so which surface a command reaches is not something a caller ever has to
think about.

**Every operation also answers `HEAD`**, with the same status and headers and no body.

**No response is cacheable, with exactly one exception.** Every operation below carries
`cache-control: no-store`. The exception is not an operation at all: this document, served at
`/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`, carries `cache-control: public, max-age=3600` and a
strong `ETag`, so a CLI can revalidate it with `If-None-Match` and get a `304`.

**Every response carries `x-request-id`** — the caller's own `x-request-id` when it sent a
well-formed one, and a fresh UUID otherwise. It is repeated in `error.request_id` on every error,
and it is the one thing worth quoting in a bug report.

**No `Link` headers.** This API never emits `Link: rel="next"`, so a client that auto-paginates on
it (restish among them) has nothing to follow. Result-set breadth is controlled by the query
parameters.

**Errors are one shape, always JSON.** Every failure below is
`{"error":{"code","message","request_id","details"?}}`, and `error.code` is the field to branch on —
it is stable, and the human-readable `message` is not. Stable means an existing code never changes its
meaning; the table below can still GROW (`rate_limited` arrived in 2.1.0), so a client that switches on
`error.code` needs a default branch — treat an unknown code by its HTTP status.

| Status | `error.code` | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | `invalid_parameter` | A required parameter is missing or empty, or the parameters were rejected. |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | The credential is missing or was refused; `details.reason` says which. |
| `403` | `forbidden` | The credential verified but may not do this — see `details.reason` below. |
| `404` | `not_found` | No such route, or no such report. |
| `422` | `upstream_error` | The export spans too many weeks or seasons. |
| `429` | `rate_limited` / `upstream_error` | A budget is exhausted — this API's own per-account one, or the data source's export metering; `Retry-After` says when to come back. |
| `500` | `internal_error` | This API failed. |
| `502` | `upstream_error` | The data behind this API failed, or could not be reached. |
| `503` | `upstream_error` / `session_provisioning` | Temporarily unavailable; `Retry-After` says when to come back. |
| `504` | `upstream_timeout` | The request did not complete in time. |

**One command per operation.** `operationId` is the command name. The taxonomy is flat
kebab-case with a family prefix — `ref-`, `team-`, `player-`, `facet-`, `signature-` — because
there are no nested command groups to hang a tree off; ten of the commands also answer to a short
alias (`leagues`, `games`, `players`, `teams`, `passing`, `receiving`, `rushing`, `defense`,
`blocking`, `special-teams`). A **required** parameter becomes a positional argument, in the order
the operation declares it; every other parameter is a `--kebab-case` flag. The `facet` leaderboards
and `ref-leagues` require nothing, so every filter on them is a flag. The rest take positionals:
`ref-players` and `team-list` take `league`; `team-overview` takes `league season`; `ref-games`
and the four `signature` commands take `league season week`; `team-summary` takes
`league season franchise-id`; the `player-` reports take `league player-id`, and seven of them
(`player-passing-concept`, `player-passing-depth`, `player-passing-pressure`,
`player-receiving-depth`, `player-rushing-direction`, `player-snaps-summary`,
`player-position-pivot`) take `league season player-id`. Each command's `--help` prints its order.

**Budgets.** Every account has a read budget and an export budget, each per minute, shared across
every operation here and across both credentials the account may hold; a `/v1` request with
`export=true` on an operation that honours it, or a `/v2` request with `format=csv`, spends an
export slot, and anything else spends a read. Every counted response — refused or not — carries
`x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset` (seconds since the Unix
epoch), so a script can slow down before it is told to; over budget is a `429` with
`error.code` `rate_limited`, `error.details.scope` naming the budget, and a `Retry-After`.
`whoami` and `logout` are never counted.

**Retries are the caller's business, and none is a reasonable choice.** Every operation here is a
read, so retrying one is safe — but an export spends its quota whether or not the attempt
succeeds, and this API never sends `Retry-After` on anything a retry would fix except `429` and
`503`. A restish-based client retries twice by default; `RSH_RETRY=0` in the environment, or
`--rsh-retry 0` on the command, makes every command a single attempt.

**Authentication.** Every operation below needs one of two credentials, described fully under
`securitySchemes`: `pffOAuth` — sign in with your PFF account in the browser, once; refresh
happens silently afterwards — or `pffApiKey` — a PFF API key, for scripts and CI, created at
www.pff.com/account/api-keys (the API-keys section of your pff.com account page). `x-cli-config`
pre-seeds the `pffOAuth` browser flow so `restish api connect` sets it up with no further input; a
second, API-key profile is a client's own to add with `restish api set` (`api configure` was the
restish v1 command). `whoami` reports what this API believes about the caller without spending
anything; `logout` ends this host's access for the credential presented.

**CSV.** 33 of the 59 operations take `?export=true` and answer `200 text/csv` with a
`Content-Disposition` attachment instead of JSON; on the other 26 the parameter is ignored and is
not declared. Ask for `Accept: application/json` even when exporting — `Accept: text/csv` is
refused with a `406`, and the CSV content type is set on the response regardless. An **unentitled**
caller gets a `200 text/csv` with an empty body rather than a `403`; see `CsvBody`.

**CSV on `/v2`.** Every `/v2` table operation takes `format=csv` (`--format csv`) and answers
`200 text/csv` with a `Content-Disposition` attachment — the same table as its JSON body, header row
of column keys, CRLF lines, RFC 4180 quoting; see `CsvTable`. `Accept` is not consulted: one
mechanism, stated here. Errors keep the JSON envelope whatever `format` asked for.

**Report columns are data-driven.** A report's stat columns are not enumerated here — which ones come
back depends on the report, the position, the query and the entitlement — so the schemas below pin
the envelope and the identity columns exactly and leave the rest to `additionalProperties`.

**Every operation shows a real response.** The example on each `200` below is an actual body — the
JSON, and the CSV where the operation exports — cut to its first few rows, from one coherent request:
the Cincinnati Bengals (franchise `7`) in the 2022 season, week 1, Joe Burrow (player `28022`) and
the Bengals' week-1 game (`23108`). Every parameter's `example` is the value that produced them, so
a request assembled from the examples returns the body shown beside it — every row of it, not just
the first three. Each example's description says exactly what was asked.

get.summary: List the leagues you can read, with their seasons and weeks
get.description:
The starting point for everything else, and the one command that takes no arguments at all. Returns
one entry per league you may view — `nfl`, `ncaa`, `aaf` and `ufl` — each carrying its seasons, its
week calendar, its named week groups, and the season, week and week group a client should fall back
to when the caller names none.

The one operation with no league-entitlement check — a signed-in caller of any tier can list the
leagues; every other operation needs a session for at least some of what it returns.

default.summary: Every league the account can read, with its seasons and weeks
default.description: `GET /v1/leagues`, with each list of rows cut to its first 3 entries. The live response carries every row.

get.summary: List game results for a league, season and week
get.description:
`league`, `season` and `week` are all required, and restish takes them as positional arguments in
that order — `restish pff games nfl 2025 1`. One row per game: kickoff time, the home and away
franchise ids, the final score, the venue id and how far the game has been charted. Use a row `id`
as `--game` on any `facet-` command. This is the one command whose week is a single number rather
than a list; `--franchise` narrows it to one team.

default.description: `GET /v1/games?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1`, with each list of rows cut to its first 3 entries. The live response carries every row.

get.summary: Search the player directory by name or id
get.description:
`league` is required and taken as the positional argument — `restish pff players nfl --name
mahomes`. One row per player: id, name, position, jersey number, current team, college, draft
record, and height and weight in inches and pounds. `--name` is a free-text search and `--id` an
exact lookup; give one of the two, or the request is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`. Use a row
`id` as the player positional on any `player-` command.

`name` is forwarded upstream as `q`.

x-requires-one-of.message: Give name to search, or id for an exact lookup

default.description: `GET /v1/players?league=nfl&name=burrow`, complete.

get.summary: List a season's teams, franchise groups and schedule
get.description:
`league` is required and taken as the positional argument — `restish pff team-list nfl --season
2025`; without `--season` the teams span every era. Three collections in one body: `teams` (the
season's franchises with their colours and abbreviations), `franchise_groups` (the conference and
division tree they hang off) and `games` (the season's whole schedule, trimmed to id, both franchise
ids, week and kickoff). Use a `franchise_id` from here as `--franchise` anywhere else, and a game
`id` as `--game` on any `facet-` command.

default.summary: NFL, 2022 season: teams, franchise groups and schedule
default.description: `GET /v1/teams?league=nfl&season=2022`, with each list of rows cut to its first 3 entries. The live response carries every row.

get.summary: Season-to-date team report, one row per team
get.description:
`league` and `season` are required, and restish takes them as positional arguments in that order —
`restish pff team-overview nfl 2025`. One row per franchise, totalled over the weeks you ask for;
`--week` narrows the range and `--franchise` narrows it to one team. Grades are on PFF's 0-100 scale
and every other column is a raw total or rate; which columns come back depends on the league, the
query and the caller's entitlement.

default.description: `GET /v1/teams/overview?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1`, with each list of rows cut to its first 3 entries. The live response carries every row.

get.summary: Per-game team report for one franchise, one row per game

default.description: `GET /v1/teams/summary?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1&franchise_id=7`, complete.

get.summary: List the seasons a player has data for
get.description:
`league` and `player` are required, and restish takes them as positional arguments in that order —
`restish pff player-seasons nfl 4924`. The seasons a player can be asked about, so a client can
offer a season picker rather than guess. `--season` and `--week` are accepted and make no
difference: the answer is the player's whole history either way.

Returns the raw upstream payload — no report envelope.

default.description: `GET /v1/player/seasons?league=nfl&player_id=28022`, complete.

get.summary: Snap counts for a player, broken out by position
get.description:
`league`, `season` and `player` are required, and restish takes them as positional arguments in that
order — `restish pff player-snaps-summary nfl 2025 4924`. How many snaps a player took, and where.
`--week` narrows the counts to one week. This is the one command whose `snap_counts` stays a nested
object instead of being flattened into `snap_counts_*` columns.

Returns the raw upstream payload — no report envelope.

default.description: `GET /v1/player/snaps/summary?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1&player_id=28022`, complete.

get.summary: Player snap counts pivoted by position
get.description:
`league`, `season` and `player` are required, and restish takes them as positional arguments in that
order — `restish pff player-position-pivot nfl 2025 4924`. One row per position a player lined up
at, with the snaps taken there; `--week` narrows it. The only export outside the `facet` and
`signature` families: add `--export true` for the raw CSV instead of JSON.

The export returns an empty body — no header row — when the caller is not entitled; an entitled
export with no matching records still carries its header row.

With `export=true` the response is `text/csv` as an attachment named
`player_<player_id>_position_pivot_<season>.csv` instead of JSON.

200.description:
JSON report, or — when `export=true` — a CSV attachment named
`player_<player_id>_position_pivot_<season>.csv`.

Content-Disposition.description: Sent only with the `text/csv` variant. The filename is the one the report declares.

default.description: `GET /v1/player/position/pivot?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1&player_id=28022`, complete.
`GET /v1/player/position/pivot?league=nfl&season=2022&week=1&player_id=28022&export=true`, complete.

`season` stays required. `--week` narrows to one week. Grades are on PFF's 0-100 scale and every

get.summary: One of nineteen player reports for the whole league, one row per player
get.description:
Every player in one report — `passing`, `rushing`, `coverage`, `punting` and the rest — one
row per player with the report's own stat columns, league-wide: the same nineteen reports
`team-report` serves for one club, without the club. Which columns come back depends on the
report, the season and the entitlement, so `columns` names and types them per answer rather
than this document enumerating them; the three identity keys `playerId`, `player` and
`position` are always present. `season` defaults to the current season and `weekGroup` to
`REGPO`; `week` and `weekTo` narrow the group to one week or a span. The five special-teams
reports start in the 2013 season; an earlier season is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`.
Served for the NCAA the same way, over the FBS and FCS programmes the rest of the API covers.
Two slow-path outcomes, both worth a rerun or a narrower `week` span: a report whose reads run
past the minute its session credential lives may come back complete but with fewer columns
than usual (the source answers an expired credential with a partial table, not an error), and
a report that outlives its own time budget is `504 upstream_timeout`. With `format=csv` the
table streams as a file; see `CsvTable`.

The reports PFF has added its newer data points to carry them as extra columns, exactly as
`team-report` does: `pass-blocking` — `pbwr` and `truePassSetPbwr` (pass block win rate, on
all snaps and on true pass sets), `islandRate` and `islandPassBlockWinRate`, plus
`offensePosGradedRate` and `offenseNegGradedRate` (OVR POS% / OVR NEG%: the linemen's
positively / negatively graded share of the OVR grade's offensive snaps — every offensive-role
snap on a regular, pre-snap-penalty or two-point play, nullified plays in, the combined grade
with the penalty grade included — on the OL group's own switch; a TE or RB row carries them
only once his own group is released, `null` until then); `run-blocking` — `posGradedRate` and `negGradedRate`, with `zone…` and `gap…`
variants, plus the same `offensePosGradedRate` / `offenseNegGradedRate` pair; `run-defense` —
`posGradedRate` and `negGradedRate`; `pass-rush` — `doubleTeamRate`; `passing` —
`passRateOe`, `completionOe` and `accuracyOe`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and
`offenseNegGradedRate` (the QB's positively / negatively graded share of the OVR grade's
offensive snaps — nullified plays and scrambles in, penalty grade included); `receiving` — `receptionsOe`,
`receptionsOeTotal`, `linedUpVsCb`, `linedUpVsS` and `linedUpVsLb`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and
`offenseNegGradedRate` (the same pair for the receivers; served while any of the WR, TE and HB
groups is released, and a row carries them only once its own group is — `null` until then); `rushing` —
`carryShare`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and `offenseNegGradedRate` (the same pair for the
backs; a QB, WR or TE row on the rushing board carries them only once his own position group
is released, `null` until then); `field-goals` — `fieldGoalOe` and `fieldGoalOeTotal`. Rates are percentages
on the 0–100 scale at one decimal, over-expectation figures in percentage points and the
two totals in receptions and makes; a cell is `null` when the source has no rows for
the player or the rate's denominator is zero. The
graded-play rates (`pbwr`, `posGradedRate`, `negGradedRate`, `offensePosGradedRate`, `offenseNegGradedRate` and their variants) are served

`season` defaults to the current season and `weekGroup` to `REGPO`; name explicit weeks with
`weekIds` instead — the two cannot be combined. A value that does not apply is `null`, never

no rows, for a season that has not been loaded yet — NFL seasons before 2025, and every NCAA
season, at the time of writing. With `format=csv` the table streams as a file; see `CsvTable`.

Newer data points join a category as PFF releases them, so the column list can grow between
two answers. For the NFL the data-science entries — weighted EPA per play (`wepa`, and

(1 = highest; `null` whenever `opponentElo` is), and `sos` beside the table summarises the
season:
score, rank, games played and remaining, and how many games fall in each difficulty bucket.
`sos` is `null` when no strength-of-schedule source exists for the league. `season` defaults to
the current season. For NCAA programmes `sos` is always `null`, and `opponentDivision` names the
opponent's conference subdivision (`Sun Belt West`) only when the directory tracks one for that
conference — most NCAA conferences have none, so it is `null` there too. With `format=csv` the

get.summary: A team's leaders for one position group, with rank and percentile
get.description:
One row per player of the team in the chosen position group — `receiving` unless `group` says
otherwise — with every stat of that group's leaderboard and, beside each, where the value
places among the qualified players at that player's own position across the league: `targets`
then `targetsRank` (1 = best), `targetsRankOf` (how many qualified players were ranked) and
`targetsPercentile` (the share of them, 0–100, the value beats — higher is better whatever the
stat's direction), and so on. Qualified means carrying at least a fifth of the position
leader's volume in the group's headline category, the same floor the by-position reports open
on; a player below it is listed with their stats and all three placing columns `null`.
`qualification` beside the table states the rule: the volume column it is measured on and its
name in prose, the share of the position leader's volume required, and the resulting minimum
for each position. `season` defaults to the current season and `weekGroup` to `REGPO`. A stat
the source did not report for a player is `null` in all four columns. `updatedAt` is the time
this answer was produced.
For NCAA programmes the same table is served over the FBS and FCS universe; players whose
position code falls outside the group's NFL vocabulary are not listed, and a programme with
no rows in the group's facet gets an empty table rather than an error. This is one facet
read, not a multi-report fan-out, so the token backing it rarely runs out — but a read that
does span past 60 s carries the same risk as the two report operations: it may come back
with fewer columns than usual, so rerun it. With `format=csv` the table streams as a file;
see `CsvTable`.

get.summary: A team's rushing by direction, one row per rusher and gap, plus totals
get.description:
Two tables in one answer. `columns` and `rows` hold one row per rusher and run direction — the
player's id, name and position, the direction (left end to right end, then the quarterback
buckets) and the eleven direction stats: attempts, yards, yards per attempt, touchdowns, first
downs, explosive runs, yards after contact and per attempt, longest, avoided tackles, fumbles.
Rushers are ordered by total attempts, most first, so the first rows are the lead back.
`totalsColumns` and `teamTotals` hold one row per direction for the whole team. `season`
defaults to the current season and `weekGroup` to `REGPO`. Served for NCAA programmes the same
way; a programme with no rows in that source gets both tables empty rather than an error. A
report that takes longer than a minute may come back with fewer columns than usual — rerun it.
With `format=csv` the rusher × direction table streams as a file, or the team totals with
`table=totals`; see `CsvTable`.

get.summary: One of nineteen player reports for a team, one row per player
get.description:
The team's players in one report — `passing`, `rushing`, `coverage`, `punting` and the rest —
one row per player with the report's own stat columns. Which columns come back depends on the
report, the season and the entitlement, so `columns` names and types them per answer rather than
this document enumerating them; the three identity keys `playerId`, `player` and `position` are
always present. `season` defaults to the current season and `weekGroup` to `REGPO`; `week` and
`weekTo` narrow the group to one week or a span. The five special-teams reports start in the
2013 season; an earlier season is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`. Served for NCAA
programmes the same way; a report with no rows for the programme in its section comes back
as an empty table, never an error. Two slow-path outcomes, both worth a rerun or a narrower
`week` span: a report whose reads run past the minute its session credential lives may come
back complete but with fewer columns than usual (the source answers an expired credential
with a partial table, not an error), and a report that outlives its own time budget is
`504 upstream_timeout`. With `format=csv` the table streams as a file; see `CsvTable`.

The reports PFF has added its newer data points to carry them as extra columns:
`pass-blocking` — `pbwr` and `truePassSetPbwr` (pass block win rate, on all snaps and on true
pass sets), `islandRate` and `islandPassBlockWinRate`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and
`offenseNegGradedRate` (OVR POS% / OVR NEG%: the linemen's positively / negatively graded share
of the OVR grade's offensive snaps — every offensive-role snap on a regular, pre-snap-penalty or
two-point play, nullified plays in, the combined grade with the penalty grade included — on the
OL group's own switch; a TE or RB row carries them only once his own group is released, `null`
until then); `run-blocking` — `posGradedRate` and
`negGradedRate`, with `zone…` and `gap…` variants, plus the same `offensePosGradedRate` /
`offenseNegGradedRate` pair; `run-defense` — `posGradedRate` and
`negGradedRate`; `pass-rush` — `doubleTeamRate`; `passing` —
`passRateOe`, `completionOe` and `accuracyOe`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and
`offenseNegGradedRate` (the QB's positively / negatively graded share of the OVR grade's
offensive snaps — nullified plays and scrambles in, penalty grade included); `receiving` —
`receptionsOe`, `receptionsOeTotal`, `linedUpVsCb`, `linedUpVsS` and `linedUpVsLb`, plus `offensePosGradedRate` and
`offenseNegGradedRate` (the same pair for the receivers; served while any of the WR, TE and HB groups is
released, and a row carries them only once its own group is — `null` until then); `rushing` — `carryShare`, plus
`offensePosGradedRate` and `offenseNegGradedRate` (the same pair for the backs; a QB, WR or TE row on
the rushing board carries them only once his own position group is released, `null` until then);
`field-goals` — `fieldGoalOe` and
`fieldGoalOeTotal`. Rates are percentages on the 0–100 scale at one decimal, over-expectation
figures in percentage points and the two totals in receptions and makes; a cell is `null` when the source has no rows for
the player or the rate's denominator is zero. The graded-play rates (`pbwr`, `posGradedRate`, `negGradedRate`,
`offensePosGradedRate`, `offenseNegGradedRate` and their variants) are served for the NFL and
NCAA alike; the rest are NFL-only and absent from an
NCAA answer. A column stays out of `columns` until PFF releases it, so read `columns` rather
than assuming a list.

league.name: league
league.description:
League slug for the leaderboard commands — exactly `nfl`, `ncaa`, `hs`, `aaf` and `ufl` are
recognised; anything else is rejected. Give it with `--season`, or give `--game` alone instead (the
league is resolved from the game); a request satisfying neither is refused with `400
invalid_parameter` before anything is fetched, and a blank value counts as missing for that rule.
Access is enforced per league: a caller with view-only rights gets a `200` with fields removed and a
`restricted` key, not a `403`.

league_required.name: league
league_required.description:
League slug, and the FIRST positional argument of every command that takes one — every command
except the `facet` leaderboards, where `--league` stays a flag because `--game` alone is a complete
request. Exactly `nfl`, `ncaa`, `hs`, `aaf` and `ufl` are recognised; anything else is rejected.
Only the four configured leagues — `nfl`, `ncaa`, `aaf`, `ufl` — are ever listed by `ref-leagues`,
so `hs` is accepted here but has no discoverable metadata. Access is enforced per league: a caller
with view-only rights gets a `200` with fields removed and a `restricted` key, not a `403`.
Required: leave the positional out and restish refuses to send the request at all, and a blank value
is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter, before anything is fetched.

season.name: season
season.description:
Season, as a four-digit year. Integer-coerced by `ref-games`, the `team` family and the `player`
families, so this form is a single season — a comma-separated list does not survive the coercion.
The `facet` and `signature` families never coerce it and take a list instead; they use the
`season_list` variant. On `player-position-pivot` exports, a request spanning too many seasons is
rejected with a `422`.

season_required.name: season
season_required.description:
Season, as a four-digit year, taken as a positional argument. A single season only — this form is
integer-coerced, so a comma-separated list does not survive it. Required: leave the positional out
and restish refuses to send the request at all, and a blank value is refused with `400
invalid_parameter` naming this parameter, before anything is fetched.

season_list.name: season
season_list.description:
Season for the leaderboard commands. A four-digit year, or a comma-separated list such as
`2023,2024` — never coerced, so a list reaches the data intact. Give it with `--league`, or give
`--game` alone instead; a request satisfying neither is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` before
anything is fetched, and a blank value counts as missing for that rule. When `--game` carries the
request, a blank season instead short-circuits to an empty 200 — the recorded behaviour of the data
behind this API. On an export, a value spanning too many seasons comes back `422`.

season_list_required.name: season
season_list_required.description:
Season, and the SECOND positional argument of the four `signature` commands. A four-digit year, or a
comma-separated list of them such as `2023,2024` — the `signature` family never coerces this value,
so a list reaches the data intact. Required: leave the positional out and restish refuses to send
the request at all, and a blank value is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter,
before anything is fetched — the pattern below admits the blank string only because the shape is
shared with the optional variant. On an export, a value spanning too many seasons comes back `422`.

week.name: week
week.description:
Week filter. Never coerced except by `ref-games`, so a comma-separated list is accepted such as
`1,2,3`. `ref-games` is the one exception — it integer-coerces the value and takes the
`week_integer` variant. A present-but-empty value short-circuits `facet`/`signature` to an empty
200. On exports, a value spanning too many weeks is rejected with a `422`.

week_required.name: week
week_required.description:
Week, and the THIRD positional argument of the four `signature` commands. A week number, or a
comma-separated list such as `1,2,3` — the `signature` family never coerces this value, so a list
reaches the data intact. Required: leave the positional out and restish refuses to send the request
at all, and a blank value is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter, before
anything is fetched. On an export, a value spanning too many weeks comes back `422`.

week_integer.name: week
week_integer.description:
Week, and the THIRD positional argument of `games` — the one command that takes a single week number
rather than a comma-separated list. Required: leave the positional out and restish refuses to send
the request at all, and a blank value is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter,
before anything is fetched.

franchise_id.name: franchise_id
franchise_id.description:
Franchise (team) id. Integer-coerced by `ref-games` and the `team` family, forwarded uncoerced by
`facet`. Unlike `season` and `week` there is no list variant: nothing splits this value and no known
caller sends more than one, so a list form would be speculation. Sent as `--franchise` on the
command line and as `franchise_id` on the wire. Ids come from `ref-leagues` / `team-list`.

franchise_id_required.name: franchise_id
franchise_id_required.description:
Franchise (team) id, and the THIRD positional argument of `team-summary` — the report is
franchise-scoped, so there is no all-teams form of it. Ids come from `ref-leagues` / `team-list`.
Required: leave the positional out and restish refuses to send the request at all, and a blank value
is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter, before anything is fetched.

game_id.name: game_id
game_id.description:
Single-game filter, `facet` family only, forwarded uncoerced. It is also read by the entitlement
check, which resolves the game to its league and applies that league's restrictions — so a `game_id`
from a league you cannot access is a 403 even when `league` says otherwise. Sent as `--game` on the
command line and as `game_id` on the wire. Ids come from `ref-games`.

player_id.name: player_id
player_id.description:
Player id, taken as a positional argument. Ids come from `ref-players`. Required: leave the
positional out and restish refuses to send the request at all, and a blank value is refused with
`400 invalid_parameter` naming this parameter, before anything is fetched.

id.name: id
id.description:
Exact player-id lookup, `ref-players` only. Distinct from `player_id`, which the report families
use.

name.name: name
name.description: Free-text player-name search, `ref-players` only. Forwarded to the upstream as `q`, not as `name`.

career.name: career
career.description:
Career-aggregate toggle, on the player report operations only. Forwarded uncoerced and not validated
here — the upstream interprets it, and how it is interpreted depends on the report:

On the 13 reports whose body is a `PlayerReportSummary`, `career=true` replaces `season`: send
`league` + `career=true` + `week` + `player_id` and the body switches from
`subject`/`week_totals`/`weeks` to `subject`/`career`/`seasons`.

On the five that are not (`player-passing-concept`, `player-passing-depth`,
`player-passing-pressure`, `player-receiving-depth`, `player-rushing-direction`) it changes nothing
— the same body comes back — and `season` is still required: omitting it is a 400, with or without
`career`.

division.name: division
division.description:
NCAA division fan-out, `facet` family only, and **only honoured when `league=ncaa`** — for any other
league it is ignored entirely. Comma-separated; each element must be `fbs`, `fcs` or `lower` and
maps to a group of franchises: `fbs` covers FBS plus the all-star group, `fcs` covers FCS, and
`lower` covers D2 and D3. Any other value fails with `502 upstream_error` — the request reaches the
data behind this API and that is where it breaks. Divisions are fetched in parallel and the results
concatenated, so a multi-division request can take substantially longer than a single-division one.

export.name: export
export.description:
`--export true` — the literal string `true`, and nothing else — returns the report as `text/csv`
rather than JSON. A restish client prints the raw file under `--rsh-print b`, or you can redirect
the body to a file; asking for `-o json` instead renders the whole export as a single JSON string,
quoted and with its line breaks escaped. An unentitled request returns an empty body. Any other
value returns JSON. Exports are metered separately from reads — a request spanning too many weeks or
seasons is rejected with a `422`, and an exhausted export budget with a `429`. On
`player-position-pivot`, `--export true` alone is not enough: `--player` and `--season` must be
present too, or JSON comes back instead.

LeaguePath.name: league
LeaguePath.description:
League slug: `nfl` or `ncaa`. Anything else is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` before any
data is fetched. It is the first positional argument of every command on this surface.

SeasonQuery.name: season
SeasonQuery.description:
Season, as a four-digit year: `2006` or later, and at most one year past the current season.
Left out, the current season is used — the season turns over on 1 March, so January and February
still belong to the previous year's season. A present-but-empty or non-numeric value is refused
with `400 invalid_parameter`: a default is applied only to a parameter that was omitted.

WeekGroupQuery.name: weekGroup
WeekGroupQuery.description:
Which part of the season to cover: `REG` (regular season), `PO` (playoffs) or `REGPO` (both,
the default). Cannot be combined with `weekIds` — naming both is refused with
`400 invalid_parameter`. Echoed back on the response as `weekGroup`.

WeekIdsQuery.name: weekIds
WeekIdsQuery.description:
Comma-separated week ids to cover instead of a whole `weekGroup` — `1,2,3` is the first three
regular-season weeks. Every id must be a real week of the league's calendar; the list is
de-duplicated and put in calendar order, and the response echoes it as `weekIds` in place of
`weekGroup`. Cannot be combined with `weekGroup` — naming both is refused with
`400 invalid_parameter`.

TeamPath.name: team
TeamPath.description:
The team, as its slug (`los-angeles-rams`) or its numeric franchise id (`26`) — both resolve
through the league's team directory for the season, and both produce the same answer. Unknown
either way is refused with `404 not_found`, and `details.team` echoes what was asked. The
second positional argument of every per-team command.

WeekQuery.name: week
WeekQuery.description:
Narrow the report to one week of the `weekGroup` — or, with `weekTo`, to a span of weeks. A week
id the group does not hold is refused with `400 invalid_parameter` naming the ids it does hold.

WeekToQuery.name: weekTo
WeekToQuery.description:
The last week of a span that starts at `week`; requires `week`. A reversed span is read the
right way round. Refused with `400 invalid_parameter` when `week` is absent.

FormatQuery.name: format
FormatQuery.description:
The body's shape: `json` (the default) is the table object described under `application/json`;
`csv` streams the same table as a file — header row of the column keys, one line per row — with
`content-type: text/csv` and a `content-disposition` attachment name built from the command, the
team and the season. Metadata beside the table (`sos`, `groups`, `updatedAt`, the echoed week
span) is not in the file; ask for `json` when you need it. Errors keep the JSON envelope whatever
`format` said. Any other value is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`.

TableQuery.name: table
TableQuery.description:
Which of this operation's two tables to serve when `format=csv`: `rows` (the default) is the
rusher × direction table, `totals` the team's per-direction totals. The JSON body always carries
both. Refused with `400 invalid_parameter` for any other value.

PositionReportPath.name: report
PositionReportPath.description:
Which report: `offense`, `passing`, `passing-depth`, `passing-pressure`, `receiving`,
`receiving-depth`, `rushing`, `blocking`, `pass-blocking`, `run-blocking`, `defense`,
`run-defense`, `pass-rush`, `coverage`, `special-teams`, `kick-returns`, `field-goals`,
`punting`, `kickoffs` — the same vocabulary as `team-report`. The second positional
argument.

TeamStatsCategory.name: category
TeamStatsCategory.description:
Which stat category the table covers. `offense-overall-success` unless set. An unknown value is
refused with `400 invalid_parameter` — the message lists the accepted ones.

TeamStatsScope.name: scope
TeamStatsScope.description:
Which teams the ranks are computed against — and which rows come back: `league` (every team,
the default), a conference (`afc`, `nfc`) or a division (`afc-east` … `nfc-west`). Conference and
division scopes are NFL-only; an unknown value is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`.

LeadersGroupQuery.name: group
LeadersGroupQuery.description:
Which position group the leaders come from — `receiving` (the default), `passing`, `rushing` or
`defense`. Anything else is refused with `400 invalid_parameter`.

TeamReportPath.name: report
TeamReportPath.description:
Which report: `offense`, `passing`, `passing-depth`, `passing-pressure`, `receiving`,
`receiving-depth`, `rushing`, `blocking`, `pass-blocking`, `run-blocking`, `defense`,
`run-defense`, `pass-rush`, `coverage`, `special-teams`, `kick-returns`, `field-goals`,
`punting`, `kickoffs`. The third positional argument. Rushing direction is its own command,
`team-rushing-direction`, because its answer is two tables.

ReportValue.description:
One report cell.

The column set is not fixed by this API: the upstream row is passed through untouched apart from
flattening the `grades` / `snap_counts` / `*_grades` sub-objects into prefixed keys —
`grades.offense` becomes `grades_offense`. Which columns a row carries therefore depends on the
report, the position, the query form and the caller's entitlement, and cannot be enumerated here.

RestrictedColumns.description:
The columns that were withheld from this response.

Present only for a caller with view-but-not-access rights on the league: only the report's
allowlisted columns are kept, and this key lists every column that was withheld. A caller with full
access never sees the key at all, so its absence is the signal that nothing was stripped — never
assume a missing column means the stat does not exist.

Every report operation can emit it. The `ref`, `team-list`, `player-seasons` and
`player-snaps-summary` operations cannot: they carry no report envelope.

ReportPlayerRow.description:
One player row of a report.

Columns are data-driven (see `ReportValue`), so only the identity columns are named. Those are the
ones the API pins: `player`, `player_id`, `position`, `team_name` and `player_game_count` lead every
per-player CSV header row, and `team`, `jersey_number`, `draft_season` and `eligible_season` are
held out of the stat columns — all nine are identity, not statistics. `status` appears on the
`game_id` query form.

Each is typed nullable: the value is the upstream row's, and nothing here guarantees it.

jersey_number.description: A string on the wire — `"09"`, `"00"`; leading zeros are meaningful.

ReportPlayerRows.description:
A report's row collection — one row per player matching the filters.

Empty (`[]`) rather than absent when there is nothing to report — the short-circuit responses still
carry the report key, with an empty array under it.

ReportTeamRow.description:
One team row of a report.

The team-level CSV header row pins `team_name`, `franchise_id` and `player_game_count` as the
leading columns and holds `season_id` out of the stat columns; everything else is data-driven (see
`ReportValue`). Used by `signature-pass-blocking-efficiency-line`, the one report with that header
row.

ReportTeamRows.description: A team report's row collection. Empty rather than absent when there is nothing to report.

CsvBody.description:
The `?export=true` body of the 33 CSV-capable operations (28 `facet`, 4 `signature` and
`player-position-pivot`): a header row of comma-separated column names, then one row per record,
CRLF-terminated. Five of the 33 answer with `CsvBodyHeaderless` instead — their report declares no
header row — and are not this shape.

**Ask for JSON, not CSV.** `Accept: text/csv` is refused with a `406` before the export is reached,
`export=true` or not. The export still arrives as `text/csv`, because the response sets that content
type itself.

oneOf.title: EntitledExport
oneOf.description: The export itself: a header row, then one row per record, CRLF-terminated.

oneOf.title: UnentitledExport
oneOf.description:
An empty body. A caller with view-but-not-access rights on this league gets a `200 text/csv` with a
`Content-Disposition` and no bytes at all, rather than a `403`. Zero bytes is therefore "you are not
entitled to this export", never "no rows matched" — an entitled export with no matching records
still carries its header row.

CsvBodyHeaderless.description:
The `?export=true` body of the five operations whose report declares no CSV header row. The export
is one blank CRLF line per record, no header row at all, and the attachment is always named
`download.csv`.

Four reports, five operations: `offense_summary`, `passing_detail`, `rushing_direction` and
`receiving_coverage` — the last backs both `facet-receiving-coverage` and
`facet-defense-coverage-matchup`.

This is a real `200 text/csv` with a real `Content-Disposition`, which is why those routes stay in
the 33: the response is well-formed, it just carries no columns. A client should say so rather than
pretend the column set exists. There is no header line to assert, so `CsvBody`'s pattern would
reject every one of them — but "no header" is not "anything": an empty column list can only ever
produce nothing at all, or CRLF-terminated blank lines, one per record. `pattern` says exactly that,
so an upstream HTML error page no longer validates as a successful export. `minLength` is still
absent on purpose: a zero-row query returns an empty file, and that is a valid answer.

A zero-byte body is indistinguishable from a headerless export with no records: both are nothing at
all. Treat an empty response from one of these five as "no columns and possibly no rows", and use
the JSON form of the operation when the difference matters.

LeagueWeek.description: One week of a league's calendar.

id.description:
Week id. Negative for preseason (Hall of Fame is -1), 1-18 regular season, 28/29/30/32 postseason on
the NFL calendar.

LeagueWeekGroup.description:
A named bundle of week ids. The five candidates are PRE, REG, PO, REGPO and AS; a group with no
weeks is dropped, so NFL has four and a league with all-star weeks has five. `default` is hard-coded
true on REGPO only.

League.description:
One league the caller may view.

Carries `id`, `name` and `abbreviation` plus `weeks`, `seasons`, `default_season`, `default_week`,
`default_week_group`, `slug` and `week_groups`. Season 2005 is withheld from `seasons` deliberately:
only a single game exists in it.

slug.description: Downcased `abbreviation` — this is the value the `league` query parameter takes.

LeaguesResponse.description:
`ref-leagues`. A `leagues` array carrying the subset of the four configured leagues — nfl, ncaa,
aaf, ufl — the caller may view. A signed-in caller of any tier gets a non-empty list, so an empty
array means the caller may view nothing, not that the service is down.

GameTeam.description: The home/away team block on a `ref-games` row.

abbreviation.description: PFF's abbreviation (six characters at NCAA scale — `BAMACT`), not the broadcast one.

color_metadata.description: Null on NFL rows; an object of colour refs on the `team-list` payload (see `DirectoryTeam`).

GameLeague.description: The league block carried inline on a `ref-games` row (`league_id` 1 = NFL, 2 = NCAA).

Game.description: One game result, passed through unshaped — this is the upstream row.

id.description: Game id — the value the `game_id` query parameter takes.

lock_status.description:
Charting state of the game: `processed` means it has been fully charted. The value set is
upstream-owned and deliberately not enumerated here.

stadium_id.description: An id only — there is no stadium lookup in this API, so there is no name to join to.

PlayerTeam.description:
A team block on a `ref-players` row, carrying `city`, `nickname`, `abbreviation`, `slug`,
`primary_color` and `secondary_color`, plus `id` from the team's `franchise_id`. Null when the
roster row's franchise has no match in the response's team list.

id.description: The franchise id — renamed from `franchise_id` by the view.

PlayerDraft.description:
Draft record. Null when the roster row has no draft, or a draft with no `franchise_id` — undrafted
players. `round` and `selection` are null on an undrafted-free-agent record (`type: "FA"`) that
still carries a season.

type.description:
`AD` is an amateur-draft entry, `FA` a free-agent one. The value set is upstream-owned and
deliberately not enumerated here.

PlayerSearchRow.description:
One `ref-players` hit. The key set is fixed — unlike the report rows, this shape is the API's own,
not the upstream's. Rows are sorted by `[last_name, first_name]`.

id.description: Player id — the value the `player_id` (and `id`) query parameters take.

jersey_number.description: A string — leading zeros are meaningful.

college.description: The college *name*, flattened from the roster row's college struct.

PlayersResponse.description:
`ref-players`. A `players` array, empty when nothing matches; the `name` query parameter reaches the
upstream as `q`.

FranchiseGroup.description:
A franchise grouping — conference, division, NCAA tier. Derived from the season's teams, and also
carried inline on each team's `groups`. `heirarchy` is the ancestor path *including* the group's own
id, outermost first — NFC East is `[6, 7]`: the conference id, then its own — and yes, the wire
really does spell it that way. NCAA nests one level deeper (tier, conference, sub-division).

DirectoryTeam.description:
One `teams[]` entry. Passed through untouched, so this is the upstream row; identity fields are
nullable because exhibition and historical franchises arrive half-filled. `groups` is the team's
full ancestor chain, not just its leaf group.

franchise_id.description: The value the `franchise_id` query parameter takes.

color_metadata.description:
The full colour set (`background_color_ref`, `helmet_color_ref`, `jersey_color_ref`, …). Keys are
upstream-owned; the values are hex colour strings.

end_season.description: `3000` on a current franchise — the upstream's open-ended sentinel.

updated_at.description:
A naive timestamp — no offset, microsecond precision. Deliberately not `format: date-time`, which it
would fail.

ShortGame.description:
A game trimmed to five fields. `team-list` reduces every game to `id`, `away_franchise_id`,
`home_franchise_id`, `week` and `start` — so a `team-list` game carries no score, no teams and no
league, and `ref-games` is where those live.

TeamsResponse.description:
`team-list`. `teams`, `franchise_groups` and `games`: the season's franchises, the grouping tree
derived from them, and the season's whole schedule trimmed to five fields. No report envelope and no
`restricted` key — this operation carries neither.

franchise_groups.description: Every group any of the returned teams belongs to, deduplicated and flattened.

TeamOverviewResponse.description:
`team-overview`. Report envelope keyed `team_overview` — one row per team.

Identity is `franchise_id`, `abbreviation` and `name`; `wins`, `losses`, `ties`, `points_scored` and
`points_allowed` are stat columns like any other and are *omitted*, not nulled, for a season that
has not kicked off.

TeamSummaryResponse.description:
`team-summary`. Report envelope keyed `team_summary` — one row per game in the requested week set,
i.e. the team's schedule with results, not a season aggregate.

PlayerSeasonsResponse.description:
`player-seasons`. Raw upstream JSON: no report envelope and no allowlisting, so there is never a
`restricted` key. Newest season first.

PlayerSnapsSummaryResponse.description:
`player-snaps-summary`. Raw upstream JSON: no report envelope, no allowlisting and no `restricted`
key. This is the ONE place `snap_counts` survives as a nested object — every report operation
flattens it to `snap_counts_*` columns, and this one does not.

snap_counts.description:
Snap totals by type — `offense`, `defense`, `special_teams`, `pass`, `pass_route`, `pass_block`,
`run`, `run_block`, `pass_rush`, `run_defense`, `coverage`, the kicking-game types. Upstream-owned,
so enumerated by example only.

PositionPivotWeekRow.description:
One week of a position's snap counts. The CSV export flattens exactly these rows and names their
columns: `position_group`, `position`, `week_id`, then the snap types.

PositionPivotPosition.description:
One alignment within a display group, with its per-week snap counts. The CSV export reaches its rows
through `positions` then `weeks`.

PositionPivotGroup.description:
One display group (QB, WR, …). There is no rollup row: group totals are summed from
`positions[].weeks[]`, which is what the CSV export does.

PositionPivotResponse.description:
`player-position-pivot` (JSON variant). Report envelope keyed `snaps`.

This is the JSON clause. The CSV needs `--export true` AND `--player` AND `--season` together; with
`--export true` but no `--player` the request falls through to here and returns JSON with a `200` —
no error, no CSV. An unentitled export returns an empty body — no header row — while this JSON still
carries the groups with their stat columns stripped; an entitled export with no matching records
still carries its header row.

PlayerReportSubject.description:
The query echo on a player summary report: who was asked about, over what, and which grade facets
the report carries. `grade_keys` names the `grades_*` columns the rows can hold.

season.description: Absent in career mode (`career=true`), present otherwise.

week.description: The requested week ids — STRINGS here, integers on the week rows.

PlayerReportGameContext.description: The game a week row belongs to. Its fields are repeated flat on the parent row.

status.description: `S` means the player started. The value set is upstream-owned and deliberately not enumerated here.

PlayerReportWeekRow.description:
One week of a player summary report: the game context (flat, and repeated as a nested `game` object)
plus that week's stat and grade columns.

PlayerReportWeekTotalRow.description:
The aggregate over the requested week set, one row per franchise the player appeared for — two rows
for a mid-season trade, each naming its `franchise_id`, and no combined row (verified live
2026-09-09 on player 63707). A single-team player gets one row.

PlayerReportSeasonRow.description:
One season of a career-mode report. `franchise_id` is an ARRAY here, not the integer it is
everywhere else: a season split across teams lists every franchise.

PlayerReportSummary.description:
A player summary report body, in one of two modes.

**Season mode** (the default): `subject`, `week_totals` (the one aggregate row over the requested
weeks) and `weeks` (one row per game).

**Career mode**: `subject`, `career` (the all-time aggregate) and `seasons` (one row per season).

The two sets do not overlap, and the mode is chosen upstream off the `career` parameter, so every
key is optional here.

Career mode replaces `season` rather than joining it: send `league` + `career=true` + `week` +
`player_id`, with no season at all. The five player reports that are NOT this shape behave
differently again: `career=true` changes nothing there, and omitting `season` is a 400.

week_totals.description:
One row per franchise represented in the requested weeks — a mid-season trade is two rows, one per
side, with no combined row; a single-team player gets one.

PlayerReportDirections.description:
The `player-rushing-direction` body: one row per rushing direction, and no `subject` block — this
path is a detail query, not one of the graded summaries.

Note the contrast with `facet-rushing-direction`, where the same `rushing_direction_stats` key holds
an ARRAY of player rows, each with its own nested `directions`.

RushingDirectionEntry.description:
One (player, direction) split — `RE`, `LT`, `LG`, `ML`, `RG`, `JS-L`, `QBSc`, … The direction
vocabulary is upstream-owned and deliberately not enumerated here.

FacetRushingDirectionRow.description:
One player of the `facet-rushing-direction` leaderboard. Identical to `ReportPlayerRow` except for
the nested `directions` array, which is why this report declares no CSV header row and exports a
headerless CSV (see `CsvBody`).

total_attempts.description:
The player's attempts across every direction. Premium-gated (it is listed in `restricted`), and not
guaranteed on the wire — consumers should fall back to the sum of `directions[].attempts`, which is
what it is derived from.

TeamDirectionRow.description:
One (franchise, direction) team split, carried under the report's second collection key.

Caveat: the `division` fan-out drops it. That form rebuilds the body from its parallel chunks under
the primary report key only — so `league=ncaa&division=…` returns `rushing_direction_stats` alone.
That same rebuild CONCATENATES the chunks without deduping, so a multi-division value repeats every
player row once per division: `division=fbs,fcs` on franchise 194 / 2024 returned 36 rows for 18
players, byte-identical in pairs, where the unnarrowed call returned 18 rows and both collections
(live-probed 2026-09-01). Send no `division` on this report.

ReceivingCoverageStats.description:
The `facet-receiving-coverage` body — three parallel row collections rather than one, which is the
whole reason this report exports a headerless CSV: a header row can only be derived from a single
list of rows.

`defenders` and `receivers` are per-player rows; `versus` is per (receiver, coverage defender)
matchup, keyed `player_id` + `coverage_player_id`.

the empty form and the populated form differ.

Column.title: Column
Column.description:
One entry per key every row carries, in the order the rows carry them. `label` is the human
heading a table renderer prints; `type` is the JSON type of a non-null cell — `integer`,
`number`, `string` or `boolean`. Any cell may also be `null`, meaning the value does not apply
or was withheld; a row never omits a key.

type.description: JSON type of a non-null cell in this column.

TeamIdentity.title: TeamIdentity
TeamIdentity.description: The team a per-team table describes — id, slug, short code and name, as the directory has them.

abbreviation.description: The short display code (`LA`), or `null` when the directory has none.

ReportRow.title: ReportRow
ReportRow.description:
One player's row of a data-driven report: the identity keys every report carries, then the
report's own stat columns, which `columns` names and types. Every value is a number, a string, a
boolean or `null` — a nested object never appears in a row.

CsvTable.title: CsvTable
CsvTable.description:
The table as a file, when `format=csv`. Four rules: the first line is the column keys in
`columns` order and every following line is one row, lines end in CRLF; a field holding a
comma, a double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes with embedded quotes doubled
(RFC 4180); a `null` cell is an empty field, booleans are `true`/`false`, numbers print exactly
as they do in the JSON body (no rounding, no thousands separators); the file is UTF-8 with no
byte-order mark. An empty table is the header line alone. Metadata that sits beside the table
in the JSON body is not in the file.

PositionReportTable.title: PositionReportTable
PositionReportTable.description:
A column with no non-null value anywhere in this answer's rows is typed `string`, whatever
the underlying stat would otherwise be — there is nothing else to infer a type from.

week.description: The week asked for, or `null` for the whole group.

TeamStatsRow.title: TeamStatsRow
TeamStatsRow.description:
One team. `teamId`, `abbreviation` and `name` are always present; every other key is a stat value
or its rank, named by `columns`. A stat that does not apply to the team is `null`, and so is a
rank the scope has no answer for.

teamId.description: The franchise id, stable across seasons.

abbreviation.description: Short team code, as the scoreboard prints it.

additionalProperties.description: A stat value (`<key>`) or its rank (`<key>Rank`), as named in `columns`.

TeamStatsTable.title: TeamStatsTable
TeamStatsTable.description:
What was asked (`league`, `season`, `category`, `scope`, and `weekGroup` or `weekIds`), when the
data was last refreshed (`updatedAt`), then the table: `columns` in header order and `rows`, one
per team, holding exactly those keys.

weekGroup.description: Present when the table covers a whole season part; absent when `weekIds` is.

weekIds.description: Present when explicit weeks were named; absent when `weekGroup` is.

updatedAt.description: When the data behind this table was last refreshed; `null` for a season not loaded yet.

TeamDirectoryGroup.title: TeamDirectoryGroup
TeamDirectoryGroup.description: One conference, division or tier the league's teams are grouped into; `parentIds` are its ancestors, outermost first.

TeamDirectoryRow.title: TeamDirectoryRow
TeamDirectoryRow.description: One team. Every key is always present; a team with no colours carries `null` in both colour columns.

abbreviation.description: The short display code (`LA`) when the directory has one, else its abbreviation; `null` when neither — the same value every per-team table's `team.abbreviation` shows.

groupIds.description: Group ids the team belongs to, joined with `;` (`11;24` — see `groups`). Empty string for none.

TeamRosterRow.title: TeamRosterRow
TeamRosterRow.description: One player, in depth-chart order. Every key is always present; a value that does not apply is `null`.

TeamScheduleSos.title: TeamScheduleSos
TeamScheduleSos.description: The season's strength-of-schedule summary — score and rank, games played and remaining, and the count of games in each difficulty bucket (`hardest` … `easiest`).

buckets.description: Count of games in each of the six fixed difficulty tiers, hardest to easiest.

TeamScheduleRow.title: TeamScheduleRow
TeamScheduleRow.description:
One week. A bye carries `isBye: true` and `null` in every game field; a game not yet played
carries `null` result and scores.

TeamLeadersRow.title: TeamLeadersRow
TeamLeadersRow.description: One player. `playerId`, `name`, `position` and `jersey` are always present; every other key is a stat value, its rank, the size of the ranked pool or its percentile, named in `columns`; a stat the source did not report is `null` in all four, and so are the three placing cells of a player below their position's qualifying volume.

TeamLeadersQualification.title: TeamLeadersQualification
TeamLeadersQualification.description:
How the table decided who counts as qualified for a placing: at least `share` of the position
leader's volume on the `key` column (`label` is that column in prose), which comes to
`minimums` — the raw floor for each position. A position missing from `minimums` had no
volume to measure, so nobody there is ranked.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The single error shape this API answers with, on every status below. `code` is the field to branch
on — it is stable, and the human-readable `message` is not. `request_id` is echoed in the
`x-request-id` response header and is what to quote in a bug report. `details` is machine-readable
context for the failure: `upstream_status` on anything that came back from the data behind this API
(`null` when there was no response at all), `parameter` on a parameter rejected before any data was
fetched, `upstream_timeout_ms` on a deadline this API imposed, `upstream` naming which data source
failed on a `502` or `504` from a `/v2` operation, and `league` and `team` on a `404` for a team
that did not resolve. It never carries an upstream body.

message.description: Human-readable, and deliberately not part of the contract.

request_id.description: Also sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

details.description: Machine-readable context. Absent when there is none.

Whoami.description:
What this API believes about the caller. `entitled` and `tier` are reported here, never enforced —
this operation itself never gates on either.

external_id.description:
The linked subscriber identity this credential resolves to, or `null` for an account with none —
every other operation refuses that account with `403 forbidden`, reason `unlinked_account`.

email.description: The account email on file, or `null`.

tier.description:
The account's subscription tier (for example `pro`, `annual`, `monthly`), or `null`. Not itself the
entitlement decision — see `entitled`.

entitled.description:
Whether this account may use the operations below. `false` is the one place this API says why a
request would be refused, rather than refusing it.

entitlement_reason.description:
Which refusal, when `entitled` is `false`; `null` when it is `true`. Mirrors the `403` error
envelope's own `details.reason` on every other operation: `subscription_required` (the account is
not PFF Pro), `trial` (a Pro free trial, which does not include this API until it converts) and
`unlinked_account` (no subscriber record at all) are different problems with different fixes, and a
bare `entitled: false` would send a paying account that is merely unlinked or on trial to the
subscribe page for something buying Pro again would not fix.

credential.description: Which security scheme the presented credential satisfied.

session_expires_at.description:
When the session this API holds for the caller next needs renewing, or `null` when no session exists
yet — this operation never creates one.

max.description: The number of devices this account may use the CLI from. Reported only — nothing enforces it yet.

BadRequest.description:
The request parameters were rejected.

`error.code` is `invalid_parameter`.

Either the request was refused before any data was fetched — a `required` parameter above was
missing or empty — or the parameters themselves were rejected. In the first case
`error.details.parameter` names the offending parameter and `error.details.upstream_status` is
`null`.

Unauthorized.description:
The credential is missing or was refused.

`error.code` is `unauthorized`.

`details.reason` names why: `missing` (no `Authorization` header at all), `malformed` (not a bearer
credential this API understands), `expired`, `invalid_signature`, `revoked`, or `wrong_token_type`
(a session token was presented — this API never accepts one). The `WWW-Authenticate` response header
is always `Bearer realm="pff-pro", error="invalid_token"`.

Forbidden.description:
The caller may not read this league or report, or may not use this API at all.

`error.code` is `forbidden`.

Four shapes share this status. Three are this API refusing the account itself and are told apart by
`details.reason`; the fourth is the upstream refusing one league or report to an account that is
otherwise entitled, which carries `details.upstream_status` and no `details.reason` at all. A
view-only league entitlement is NOT any of them: that comes back `200` with the withheld columns
listed under `restricted`, never a `403`. `subscription_required` means the credential verified but
the account is not PFF Pro — `details.tier` carries the account's tier (or `null`) and
`details.subscribe_url` where to upgrade; the message names both. `trial` means the account is on
the Pro free trial, which does not include this API until it converts to a paid plan —
`details.tier` carries it, and there is no `subscribe_url` because there is nothing left to buy.
`unlinked_account` means the account has no linked subscriber record at all — a support matter, not
a subscription one.

NotFound.description:
No such route, or no such report.

`error.code` is `not_found`.

The same envelope whichever it is.

ExportTooBroad.description:
The requested export spans too many weeks or seasons.

`error.code` is `upstream_error`.

Requests spanning too many weeks or seasons are rejected with a `422`. Narrow the `week` or `season`
list and retry; `error.details.upstream_status` is `422`.

RateLimited.description:
A read or export budget is exhausted.

`error.code` is `rate_limited`.

Two causes share this status, told apart by `error.code`. `rate_limited` is this API's own
per-account budget — so many reads a minute, so many exports a minute, across every operation here —
and `error.details.scope` says which (`api` or `export`; `verify_ip` when too many API keys were
tried from one address); `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-remaining` and `x-ratelimit-reset` (epoch
seconds) ride on every counted response, not only this one, so a client can watch its budget before
it runs out. `upstream_error` is the data source's own metering refusing an export — reads and
exports are metered separately there too — and `error.details.upstream_status` is `429`.
`Retry-After` says when to come back, on either cause.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The budget the refused request was counted against, in requests per window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window — `0` on a refusal.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: When the window resets, as seconds since the Unix epoch.

InternalError.description:
This API failed.

`error.code` is `internal_error`.

A fault in this API itself, not in the data behind it — that is reported as a `502`. Nothing of the
underlying error reaches the caller; `error.request_id` is what to quote when reporting it.

UpstreamError.description:
The data behind this API could not be reached, or failed.

`error.code` is `upstream_error`.

`error.details.upstream_status` carries the status that came back, or `null` when there never was a
response. Retryable, but not immediately.

UpstreamUnavailable.description:
A dependency this API needs is temporarily unavailable.

`error.code` is `upstream_error`.

Three causes share this status, told apart by `error.code`. `upstream_error` covers export metering
that failed closed, and the identity provider being unreachable while verifying a credential or
reading an account — both are retryable service states, not faults. `session_provisioning` means
this API is still setting up a session for a caller signing in for the first time, or after a long
gap — retrying is the intended way to wait it out, never a sign of a broken request. `Retry-After`
says how long, on every cause.

UpstreamTimeout.description:
The request did not complete in time.

`error.code` is `upstream_timeout`.

The `facet` family is allowed substantially longer than the rest, because an NCAA `division` fan-out
genuinely runs long. `error.details.upstream_timeout_ms` carries the deadline that fired when this
API imposed it.

CsvContentDisposition.description:
Present only when `format=csv`:
`attachment; filename="<operationId[-selector]>_<league>[_<team|scope>]_<season>[_<weekGroup>|_<weekIds joined by ->].csv"`.
`team-directory` has neither a team nor a scope, so that segment is omitted —
`team-directory_nfl_2025.csv`. Only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` survive in the name; anything else becomes `-`.
